label: Keep the winter passage open
proof: Control the founding state, keep its supply route functioning, and deliver one support-equipment shipment to a named partner.
success: A second highland mustering allotment and a permanent clan agreement.
failure: The affected clan withdraws offensive service until a repaired route is held for 90 days.

label: Deliver the river relief convoy
proof: A named aid agreement, an open route, and the actual equipment shipment arrive.
success: A durable rescue agreement and an additional engineer allotment.
failure: The partner withdraws its transit guarantee and the failed aid receipt cannot be reused.

label: Complete the first civil settlement
proof: Deliver housing construction, keep civilian reception within capacity, and preserve a lawful resident policy.
success: A civilian-capacity improvement and integrated Earth volunteer recruitment.
failure: Local communities withhold recruitment until reception or housing is repaired.

label: Keep an evacuation passage safe
proof: A named civilian convoy route remains open and its actual survivors reach the receiving state.
success: A rescue compact and additional marine replacement capacity.
failure: The loss is recorded by the transport owner, and the colony must repair its damaged neutrality or guarantee.

label: Honor the house naval pledge
proof: A committed fleet or marine contingent supports the named defense operation and returns with a valid service receipt.
success: A house agreement and later fleet modernization access.
failure: The affected house withdraws its next contribution and disputes central command.

label: Survive the first warm season
proof: Maintain supply, complete an adaptation program, and keep a functioning cold reserve at home.
success: Reduce the worst outside-climate penalty and unlock a second finite yeti allotment.
failure: Replacement throughput falls until the settlement has completed a 90-day supply repair.

label: House the arriving guests
proof: Deliver a real reception project and complete one valid integration or onward-resettlement outcome.
success: More civilian capacity and a trusted civil-partner relationship.
failure: Overcrowding remains visible and blocks new voluntary admissions until repaired.

label: Finish the contracted defense works
proof: Complete the agreed actual buildings in the named state and provide its promised garrison or repair service.
success: Payment, a trusted-contract receipt, and a heavy-company replacement allotment.
failure: Forfeit the unearned payment and open a contract dispute instead of generating free resources.

label: Keep the frontier oath
proof: Honor the named non-aggression and civilian-protection terms while holding the border.
success: A durable independence agreement and access to the exceptional good alliance when other conditions hold.
failure: The oath is recorded as broken and the rare route closes for that political generation.

label: Complete the salvage commission
proof: A real damaged or captured equipment lot is assigned, repaired, and delivered to its recorded client.
success: Payment and one engineer reinforcement allotment.
failure: Lose the unpaid balance and retain responsibility for any diverted equipment.

label: Hold the agreed pass
proof: Keep a named controlled mountain state supplied and honor its passage agreement.
success: A second replacement allotment and stronger northern diplomatic ties.
failure: The client withdraws support and the affected hold refuses another distant deployment.

label: Deliver the mountain service
proof: A named host completes a reachable defense or siege contract without abandoning the home supply route.
success: Payment and a clan agreement for another finite host.
failure: A chief contests the ruler and blocks new offensive contracts until arbitration.

label: Return the contracted fleet
proof: Complete one reachable naval-support contract and return the committed ships or surviving crews to a valid port.
success: Payment, a repair agreement, and a limited marine replacement allotment.
failure: Losses remain real and the captains can refuse another patron contract.

label: Restore the ash frontier depot
proof: Repair actual industry and supply in the founding or acquired frontier state without destroying the settlement workforce.
success: Permanent workshop capacity and one heavy replacement allotment.
failure: Offensive reinforcements remain restricted and a patron can demand a costly exclusive contract.

label: Preserve the expedition host
proof: Keep a viable supplied giant force and complete the cold sanctuary works.
success: One additional finite giant replacement tranche and an accepted sanctuary.
failure: The homeland refuses further offensive musters until the supply failure is repaired.

label: Contain the first growth zone
proof: Keep the declared habitat within the admitted state and complete any required resident agreement or safe movement.
success: Defensive growth benefits and a second mycid allotment.
failure: A neighboring community dispute and reduced recognition until the boundary is repaired.

label: Complete the controlled project
proof: Deliver a named equipment and construction commitment, keep the project state secure, and resolve its declared safety condition.
success: One selected support capability, not a random bundle of universal modifiers.
failure: The actual project is suspended and its resources remain spent. Any harm requires its own proven consequence receipt.

label: Keep the flame works operating
proof: Maintain real military production, a functioning supply route, and an admitted workforce in the home state.
success: One flame-host replacement tranche and improved workshop throughput.
failure: The host must choose a costly patron shipment or a 90-day repair pause.

label: Refit a proven naval prize
proof: A real captured or transferred hull receipt, a functioning port, and committed repair capacity.
success: Return the actual repaired ship to service once.
failure: The ship remains unavailable and the uncompleted refit does not create replacement vessels.

label: Reach the threatened settlement
proof: A named ally remains viable and the committed riders reach the legal front or support position.
success: A fulfilled defense receipt and an additional remount allotment.
failure: The commitment is broken and the next client demands stronger guarantees.

label: Unify the divided officers
proof: Resolve both competing patron demands and keep the founding host under one declared command.
success: A stable command and one black-orc replacement tranche.
failure: A named officer faction defects with its actual units or begins a bounded internal conflict.

label: Protect the exposed delegation
proof: Maintain the named safe route and resolve a real threatened-envoy incident.
success: Recognition or a stronger limited contract.
failure: The court loses that diplomatic channel and must decide whether to reveal more of itself.

label: Secure the host refuge
proof: Hold a supplied defensible state and complete its shelter project.
success: One additional troll allotment and a stable local command.
failure: Offensive service stops until a viable refuge is recovered.

label: Complete the siege chief's pledge
proof: Capture or defend the named actual objective under a legal contract and provide the promised settlement afterward.
success: A stable chief agreement and a finite siege replacement allotment.
failure: The chief contests the crown and removes its own surviving contingent from offensive service.

label: Keep the gate commitment
proof: Hold the named fortified state and fulfill or lawfully renegotiate its passage terms.
success: A fortress replacement allotment and stronger authority over the garrison.
failure: The patron or neighboring state can challenge the commander's claim and the garrison loses external support.

label: Honor the ancient sanctuary
proof: Protect the named refuge and complete its civilian and supply obligations without a forced levy.
success: A trusted alliance and access to one additional giant allotment.
failure: The giants withdraw service and can abandon the patron agreement.

label: Keep the remote watch supplied
proof: Maintain the named port chain and deliver one real supply or rescue shipment.
success: A stronger watch compact and a limited marine or reef-troll allotment.
failure: A remote station withdraws support until its route is restored.

label: Protect the grove communities
proof: Keep a named protected state safe and complete its resident and supply commitments.
success: One guardian replacement allotment and a durable protection agreement.
failure: Foreign service pauses until the home protection obligation is repaired.

label: Complete the exposed-island defense
proof: Build the promised coastal works, keep the port supplied, and commit the named reserve.
success: A common-defense agreement and a finite marine allotment.
failure: The neglected island refuses the next central levy until its defenses are repaired.

label: Reconcile the expedition rolls
proof: Complete administration and housing, resolve the military-civil authority dispute, and preserve actual population accounting.
success: A stable government and a choice of further conventional reinforcement or civilian development.
failure: A political faction withholds resources until its constitutional dispute is resolved.

label: Supply the winter administration
proof: Maintain two actual settled or treaty-linked cold positions and deliver their supply commitments.
success: A yeti or snow-goblin replacement allotment and a stable winter charter.
failure: A local authority suspends levies and can reject a proposed union.

label: Keep the mammoth route viable
proof: Maintain the real cold supply corridor and complete its depots without overcommitting the host.
success: A mammoth or ice-ogre replacement tranche and a chief agreement.
failure: The affected chief withdraws offensive service until the corridor is restored.

label: Honor the coastal defense pledge
proof: Protect the named port or convoy route and return the committed force according to its terms.
success: A durable sea-clan compact and a finite marine replacement allotment.
failure: A captain withdraws its surviving ships from central service.

label: Return from the winter contract
proof: Complete a named service term and return a viable supplied host to a cold refuge.
success: A trusted contract and a finite frost-troll allotment.
failure: The host refuses further foreign service until the failed obligation is repaired.
